questions.question: You see the traffic circle ahead sign. As you approach, another vehicle is already in the circle coming from your right. What is the correct action?

options.text: Enter the circle quickly before the vehicle reaches your side.
Yield to the vehicle already in the circle and only enter when it is safe.
Stop completely before entering, even if the circle is empty.

questions.question: You see the gentle curve ahead to the right warning sign while travelling at the speed limit. What is the safest response?

options.text: Maintain your speed but keep a firm grip on the steering wheel to follow the curve smoothly.
Accelerate slightly to reduce steering effort through the curve.
Move into the opposite lane to straighten your path through the curve.

questions.question: You see the sharp bend ahead warning sign while driving at the speed limit. What is the safest action?

options.text: Reduce speed before entering the bend; keep to your lane, and steer smoothly through it.
Maintain your speed and brake hard once you are inside the bend.
Accelerate slightly while turning to prevent the car from sliding.

questions.question: When approaching a hairpin bend ahead to the left warning sign, what must you do?

options.text: Drive at normal speed, but steer harder when the bend comes.
Reduce your speed well in advance and keep as far left as safely possible.
Overtake slow vehicles to avoid being stuck behind them in the bend.

questions.question: You see a winding road ahead starting to the right warning sign while driving. What is the safest action?

options.text: Accelerate before the first bend so you can clear all the bends faster.
Reduce speed and prepare to steer carefully through a series of bends.
Keep right on the roadway to get a better line through the bends.

questions.question: When you see a combined curve warning sign, what does it mean and how should you respond?

options.text: Two sharp curves are close together, so slow down and keep to your side of the road.
Only one bend is ahead, so you can drive normally.
The road may be slippery, so you must stop before the bend.

questions.question: You are driving on a freeway and you see a two-way traffic ahead warning sign. What does this mean?

options.text: Overtaking is encouraged, as both sides have equal space.
The road will no longer be divided; oncoming traffic will be using the same roadway.
The road is merging into one-way traffic going in your direction only.

questions.question: You are driving on a rural road and see a two-way traffic crossroad ahead warning sign. What does it tell you?

options.text: Only one-way traffic will cross your path, so you don't need to look both ways.
You are on a two-way road, and another road will cross it, so vehicles may approach from the left, right, ahead, or opposite.
The road ahead is about to become a one-way street, and cross traffic must yield to you.

questions.question: You are driving in the right-hand lane and see a right lane ends warning sign ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Increase speed and try to overtake all vehicles on the left before the lane ends.
Continue in your lane until it completely disappears, then force your way left.
Signal early, adjust your speed, and merge safely into the left lane.

questions.question: You see a concealed driveway to the right warning sign while driving on a suburban road. What must you be especially careful about?

options.text: Vehicles may unexpectedly enter or cross your path from a hidden entrance on the right.
The road will curve sharply to the right, so you must reduce speed.
You are approaching a tollgate and must prepare to stop.

questions.question: You see a concealed driveway to the left and right warning sign. What must you anticipate?

options.text: Hidden entrances on both sides where vehicles may unexpectedly join the road.
That the road surface will suddenly become uneven.
That the lanes are ending and you must merge into one.
